4.1: Krishna reveals the lineage: I taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvan, who told Manu, who told Ikshvaku.
4.2: Handed down through the royal sages, this yoga was lost to the world over long ages.
4.3: That same ancient yoga I declare to you today, because you are My devotee and friend — it is the supreme secret.
4.4: Arjuna's honest objection: you were born later than Vivasvan — how could you have taught him?
4.5: Many births have passed for both of us; I know them all, you do not.
4.6: Though unborn and imperishable, the Lord of beings takes birth through His own power.
4.7: Whenever dharma declines and adharma rises, I manifest Myself.
4.8: To protect the good, destroy the wicked and re-establish dharma, I am born in every age.
4.9: One who truly knows My divine birth and action is not reborn on leaving the body, but comes to Me.
4.10: Freed from attachment, fear and anger, purified by knowledge, many have attained My being.
4.11: However people approach Me, so I receive them; all paths lead to Me.
4.12: Those desiring quick success worship the gods, because results from action come swiftly in this world.
4.13: The fourfold order was created by Me according to quality and action; though its author, know Me as changeless.
4.14: Actions do not taint Me, nor do I long for their fruit; one who knows this is not bound by action.
4.15: The ancients, knowing this, performed action; do likewise, as they did in olden times.
4.16: Even the wise are confused about action and inaction; I will teach you the action that frees you from evil.
4.17: One must understand action, wrong action and inaction — the way of action is deep and hard to fathom.
4.18: The famous paradox: one who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is wise among people.
4.19: Whose undertakings are free from desire and motive, whose actions are burnt by the fire of knowledge — the wise call that person learned.
4.20: Abandoning attachment to results, ever content and dependent on nothing, such a one does nothing though engaged in action.
4.21: Free of expectation, mind and self controlled, giving up all possessions, doing only bodily action, one incurs no sin.
4.22: Content with what comes unsought, beyond the pairs of opposites, free of envy, even in success and failure — not bound though acting.
4.23: For one free from attachment, liberated, mind fixed in knowledge, acting as sacrifice — all action melts away.
4.24: The offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, offered by Brahman into the fire of Brahman.
4.25: Some yogis offer sacrifice to the gods; others offer the self as sacrifice in the fire of Brahman.
4.26: Some offer hearing and the senses into the fire of restraint; others offer sound and objects into the fire of the senses.
4.27: Others offer all the functions of the senses and the breath into the fire of self-control kindled by knowledge.
4.28: Some sacrifice with wealth, austerity or yoga; others with study and knowledge, keeping strict vows.
4.29: Others offer the outgoing breath into the incoming, and the incoming into the outgoing, restraining both.
4.30: Others regulate diet and offer breath into breath; all these know sacrifice, and sacrifice destroys their impurities.
4.31: Those who eat the remnant of sacrifice attain the eternal; this world is not for the one who does not sacrifice.
4.32: Many kinds of sacrifice are set forth in the Vedas; know them all as born of action, and knowing this, you will be free.
4.33: Knowledge-sacrifice is superior to material sacrifice; all action in its entirety culminates in knowledge.
4.34: How to learn it: approach the wise with humility, ask questions and serve — the seers of truth will teach you.
4.35: Knowing this, you will not fall into delusion again; you will see all beings in yourself and then in Me.
4.36: Even if you were the worst of sinners, you would cross all evil by the raft of knowledge.
4.37: As kindled fire turns wood to ashes, so the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes.
4.38: Nothing here purifies like knowledge; one perfected in yoga finds it in the Self in time.
4.39: The faithful, devoted and sense-controlled attain knowledge, and having attained it, reach supreme peace at once.
4.40: The ignorant, faithless and doubting perish; for the doubting there is neither this world nor the next nor happiness.
4.41: One who has renounced action through yoga and cut doubt by knowledge, established in the Self, is not bound.
4.42: Therefore cut with the sword of knowledge this doubt born of ignorance that dwells in your heart — take refuge in yoga and stand up.
